summary: Khao man gai (ข้าวมันไก่) is Bangkok's everyday chicken-rice plate: poached chicken over rice cooked with chicken fat and broth, usually with cucumber, a bowl of clear soup and a tangy ginger-chilli fermented-soybean sauce. Pratunam is a useful area to try it; Go-Ang Kaomunkai Pratunam is a long-running, Michelin-recognised example, though you can find versions across the city.
whyGo: It is a simple, satisfying way to taste a Thai take on Hainanese chicken rice, with the sauce supplying the sharp, savoury character.
The mild chicken and rice can suit diners who prefer less chilli, since the heat is often added through a separate sauce.
Pratunam has long-established chicken-rice specialists as well as many casual stalls, so this can be an easy lunch stop while exploring the district.
bestFor: Travellers seeking an affordable everyday Bangkok meal
Chicken-rice fans interested in comparing Thai sauces and rice
A quick lunch near Pratunam shopping areas
skipIf: You avoid chicken, animal fat or chicken stock
You need guaranteed allergen control or a fully vegetarian meal
A basic casual stall meal is less appealing than a destination restaurant
duration: Allow 30–60 minutes for a meal, including possible queues at a popular shop; this is a planning estimate.
cost: No current price for the Pratunam stall was verified. Allow around THB 60–150 per plate as a planning estimate; extras, larger portions and air-conditioned branches may cost more. Check the menu before ordering.
hours: Go-Ang Kaomunkai Pratunam is listed by the Tourism Authority of Thailand, but its current daily hours were not available in the listing reviewed. Hours vary by shop; check the chosen stall's current listing or call before setting out.
bestTime: Try a chicken-rice stall around lunch, but arrive earlier at popular shops in case food sells out. For Go-Ang, confirm opening hours first; no December 2026 schedule was posted.
gettingThere: The Tourism Authority of Thailand lists Go-Ang Kaomunkai Pratunam at 960–962 Soi Phetchaburi 30, Ratchathewi. Use that address to navigate from your current Bangkok location; the Pratunam district is served by nearby city rail stations, followed by a walk or short taxi ride.
booking: This is generally a casual walk-in meal; no reservation details were found for the Pratunam stall. Go-Ang's TAT listing gives telephone +66 2 252 6325. It lists cash payment, so carry some baht.
accessibility: Step-free entry, accessible toilet, seating clearance and accessible routes were not verified. Casual street-side shops may have narrow or uneven approaches; contact the chosen venue if access is essential.
practicalTips: Ask for khao man gai (ข้าวมันไก่); some stalls also serve fried chicken with rice, a separate variation.
The sauce usually contains fermented soybeans, ginger and chilli. It may be served on the side, but confirm if you need low spice or have dietary restrictions.
Some versions include chicken offal or blood cubes; ask what is included and request plain chicken if preferred.
The TAT listing describes Go-Ang's rice cooked with chicken oil and its double-boiled soup; it also says the venue accepts cash.
decemberNotes: Khao man gai is an everyday dish rather than a seasonal event. No special December 2026 hours were found; confirm each shop's holiday schedule, especially around Christmas and New Year.
uncertainties: Current Go-Ang menu prices and opening hours were not verified from a live operator source.
Queue times, payment methods beyond Go-Ang's TAT listing, and holiday opening can change.
Ingredients, sauce heat, allergens, fried-chicken availability and accessibility differ by vendor.
